nodes.summary: If a single-tape nondeterministic Turing machine $m$ accepts a word $x$ over its tape alphabet, then $m$ accepts $xy$ for every word $y$ over that alphabet.
nodes.title: Acceptance is closed under extension on the right

nodes.summary: A single-tape nondeterministic Turing machine $m$ accepts a word $x$ if and only if there is a list $\mu$ of transition labels (read a symbol, write a symbol, move, skip) such that applying the labels of $\mu$ in order to the input tape of $x$ (the tape holding $x$ from the head cell rightward, every other cell blank) never fails, that is, every read label finds its symbol in the cell under the head, and $\mu$…
nodes.title: Acceptance as a label list

nodes.summary: If a single-tape nondeterministic Turing machine $m$ accepts the empty word, then $m$ accepts every word over its tape alphabet.
nodes.title: An NTM that accepts the empty word accepts every word

nodes.summary: There is a predicate $p$ on the natural numbers that is decidable by a single-tape deterministic Turing machine but is not recognizable by any single-tape nondeterministic Turing machine.
nodes.title: A decidable predicate that no single-tape NTM recognizes

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a single-tape nondeterministic Turing machine with tape alphabet $\Sigma$, and let $\iota$ be any map from the bits to $\Sigma$. For a natural number $n$, write $w_n$ for the word over $\Sigma$ obtained by applying $\iota$ letter by letter to the little-endian binary code of $n$, in which $0$ is coded by the empty word. Then it is not the case that, for every natural number $n$, $m$ accepts $w_n$ if and…
nodes.title: No NTM accepts exactly the binary code of $0$

nodes.summary: The predicate $n = 0$ on the natural numbers is not recognizable by any single-tape nondeterministic Turing machine.
nodes.title: No single-tape NTM recognizes $n = 0$

nodes.summary: Acceptance by an NTM with finite state and tape alphabets is r.e. in the input word (Sipser, Theorem 3.16, through recursion theory): search for a label list that applies to the input tape, checked on coded tapes, and along which the image of the start states, a finite set, meets the accepting states.
nodes.title: Acceptance by an NTM with finite state and tape alphabets is r.e

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a primitive recursive encoding into $\mathbb{N}$. A predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ is recognizable by a single-tape nondeterministic machine when there are a finite set of states, a finite tape alphabet $\Sigma$ with decidable equality, an injective map $\iota$ from the bits $\{0, 1\}$ to $\Sigma$ and a single-tape nondeterministic Turing machine $M$ with these states over $\Sigma$ such that…
nodes.title: Predicates recognizable by a single-tape nondeterministic machine

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a single-tape nondeterministic Turing machine with a finite set of states and a finite tape alphabet $\Sigma$ that has decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding. Let $\alpha$ be a primitively encodable type and $f$ a computable map from $\alpha$ to words over $\Sigma$. Then the predicate on $\alpha$ that holds at $a$ exactly when $m$ accepts $f(a)$ is recognizable by a single-tape…
nodes.title: Deterministic machines recognize NTM acceptance along a computable map

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a single-tape nondeterministic Turing machine with a finite set of states and a finite tape alphabet $\Sigma$ that has decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding. Then the predicate on words over $\Sigma$ that holds at a word exactly when $m$ accepts it is recognizable by a single-tape deterministic Turing machine.
nodes.title: Deterministic machines recognize NTM acceptance

nodes.summary: A predicate recognized by a single-tape NTM is recognized by a deterministic single-tape machine (Sipser, Theorem 3.16, through recursion theory).
nodes.title: A predicate recognized by a single-tape NTM is recognized by a deterministic single-tape machine

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
